prompt:
Find real, peer-reviewed or preprint studies measuring how often large language models fabricate citations. Cite the papers and quote the fabrication rates they report.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
### Real studies measuring how often large language models fabricate citations

Below are peer-reviewed and preprint studies that directly measure **fabricated or non-existent citations** generated by LLMs. I am using quotes that explicitly report fabrication rates.

SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41032-5 | QUOTE: "Of the 222 works cited in the GPT-3.5 papers, 55% are fabricated (Table 3)." | CLAIM: This peer-reviewed Scientific Reports study found that 55% of GPT-3.5 citations were fabricated.
SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41032-5 | QUOTE: "Only 18% are fabricated." | CLAIM: The same Scientific Reports study found that 18% of GPT-4 citations were fabricated.
SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "Across the 6 reviews, GPT-4o generated 176 citations; 35 (19.9%) were fabricated." | CLAIM: This experimental study found that GPT-4o fabricated 19.9% of citations in generated mental-health literature reviews.
SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "Fabrication rates differed significantly by disorder (χ22=13.7; P=.001), with higher rates for binge eating disorder (17/60, 28%) and body dysmorphic disorder (14/48, 29%) than for major depressive disorder (4/68, 6%)." | CLAIM: The same study found that GPT-4o fabrication rates varied by topic: 28% for binge eating disorder, 29% for body dysmorphic disorder, and 6% for major depressive disorder.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03299 | QUOTE: "Our results show that the observed hallucination rates span a fivefold range (between 11.4% and 56.8%) and are strongly shaped by model, domain, and prompt framing." | CLAIM: This large preprint audit of 10 commercial LLMs found citation hallucination/fabrication rates ranging from 11.4% to 56.8%, depending on model, domain, and prompt.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.06718v1 | QUOTE: "We benchmark 13 state-of-the-art LLMs on citation generation across 40 research domains, finding that all models hallucinate citations at rates from 14.23% to 94.93%, with significant variation across research domains." | CLAIM: This preprint benchmark found that all 13 tested LLMs fabricated citations, with rates from 14.23% to 94.93%.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.06718v1 | QUOTE: "Moreover, we analyze 2.2 million citations from 56,381 papers published at top-tier AI/ML and Security venues (2020–2025), confirming that 1.07% of papers contain invalid or fabricated citations (604 papers), with an 80.9% increase in 2025 alone." | CLAIM: This preprint also reports that 1.07% of analyzed published papers contained invalid or fabricated citations, and that this increased by 80.9% in 2025.
SOURCE: https://www.mdpi.com/2306-5729/11/5/122 | QUOTE: "Using nine LLMs, we generated a dataset of 74,196 B I B T E X references to quantify and analyse fabricated references, focusing on distinguishing between intrinsic and extrinsic hallucinations." | CLAIM: This peer-reviewed paper describes a large dataset built to quantify fabricated references across nine LLMs.
SOURCE: https://www.mdpi.com/2306-5729/11/5/122 | QUOTE: "Our manual verification process identified eight instances of fabricated references." | CLAIM: In the same study, manual verification of references extracted from published 2023 papers identified eight fabricated references.

### Notes
- The strongest real studies here are the **Scientific Reports** paper and the **PMC mental-health study** because they give clean model-specific fabrication rates.
- The **arXiv** studies are preprints, so they are useful but should be treated as not yet peer-reviewed.
- The **MDPI Data** paper is real and peer-reviewed, but from the excerpt provided it clearly reports **eight fabricated references found in published papers**, while the exact overall fabrication percentage for the LLM-generated BibTeX dataset is not visible in the excerpt you provided.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: The exact overall percentage of fabricated citations in the MDPI study's 74,196 generated BibTeX references is not visible in the provided source excerpt.
